caption.instagram:
You saved six months of spending on one income. Why does a couple's same rule last longer?

Two households follow the same rule. A couple each earn €2,500 a month after tax and spend €3,600; a single earner takes home €3,000 and spends €2,400. One job is lost in each.

The couple is €1,100 a month short, so their fund lasts nearly 20 months. The single earner is short the full €2,400, and hers lasts 6. Take the couple's second pay away as well and they are back to six: the extra time came from an income that survived, not from the rule.

That second income sits quietly inside several rules of thumb. On one income, many people aim for the upper end of the emergency fund range or beyond, often six to twelve months, depending on how steady the income is and how long new work would take to find.
